title: Maharashtra Exam Paper Leak: Reform Panel Proposes 10 Years In Jail, Rs 10 Crore Fine
description: Maharashtra Exam Paper Leak: The committee has recommended amendments to the Maharashtra Competitive Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to incorporate stricter provisions.
author: Prajakta Prabhakar Pol, Rahul Kumar
content:
Maharashtra Exam Paper Leak: The examination reform committee constituted by the Maharashtra government has recommended stringent penalties for those found guilty of leaking question papers in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) recruitment examinations.
Those found involved in leaking examination papers will face seven to 10 years in prison. Additionally, a minimum fine of Rs 10 crore will be imposed, along with the confiscation of property.
The committee has recommended amendments to the Maharashtra Competitive Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to incorporate stricter provisions. A bill proposing these amendments is expected to be tabled during the upcoming Winter Session of the Maharashtra Legislature.
Earlier, the Maharashtra government had ordered a probe into alleged malpractice and question paper leaks in nine examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), inviting candidates, students, and other stakeholders to submit evidence by November 16, 2026.
According to a press release issued by the Commission of Inquiry for MPSC Examinations, the panel was tasked with investigating allegations of malpractice, including the leakage of question papers, answer keys or parts thereof, in examinations conducted between 2023 and 2026.
In August this year, the Maharashtra Public Service Commission cancelled the entire recruitment process for Drug Inspector, Group-B posts under the Food and Drug Administration Department following allegations of a question paper leak.

title: Akhilesh Yadav Adds Insult To Injury, Congress Fumes As BJP Takes Potshots
description: Sources say that Congress is upset with SP unilaterally announcing five candidates even as the seat-sharing talks remained deadlocked
author: Mohit Babbar, Mohd Asim
content:
The Congress-Samajwadi Party (SP) seat-sharing talks appear to be heading into rough weather, with the SP going ahead and announcing five candidates for the upcoming elections even as negotiations with the Congress remain deadlocked.
Sources have told NDTV that the SP's unilateral move has left Congress leaders fuming, with many seeing it as an insult added to injury. The SP had initially offered the Congress a mere 26 seats in response to its demand for over 100, after the party had already scaled down its original demand of 181 seats. Now, the announcement of five candidates in the middle of the negotiations has further angered Congress leaders in Uttar Pradesh, who are planning to take up the issue with the party high command.
What has particularly upset the Congress is that four of the five candidates announced are from western Uttar Pradesh, including Saharanpur, the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Congress UP working president Imran Masood.
The five candidates announced by the SP are Umar Ali from Behat, Aashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana, Mahbub Ali from Amroha - all sitting MLAs from western UP - and Jyoti Lodi from Lalitpur in Jhansi. The four western UP constituencies have substantial Muslim and Dalit populations, a combination the Congress has been eyeing as part of its revival strategy. The Congress was reportedly eyeing two of these four seats.
Imran Masood hit out at the SP questioning party's seriousness about the alliance. "How can they release names even before the talks are finalised". He added that even Congress can name candidates from the same seats.
"We are not beggars. We are not waiting to get some charity from Akhilesh Yadav. How can he treat us like this?" an angry Masood said.
Congress sources have told NDTV that the party would not "bow down to pressure tactics" or accept any "dictatorship".
Read | Akhilesh Yadav's Open Letter, Then A Move That Overlaps Congress Wishlist
The surprise move by the SP came after party chief Akhilesh Yadav posted what appeared to be an open letter calling for a better understanding between the allies over seat-sharing.
Describing the upcoming elections as a "historic opportunity" to dethrone the BJP, Yadav called for "serious talks", taking public expectations and political realities into account.
"We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our 'alliance' wins in most constituencies. Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he said in a post on X.
The BJP, meanwhile, has seized the opportunity to take potshots at the Congress-SP tussle.
कथनी और करनी में फ़र्क़ देखिए! माननीय अखिलेश जी कांग्रेस को लिखते हैं: "सीट बंटवारा नहीं, सीट समायोजन", "उम्मीदवार थोपे नहीं जाएंगे", हर प्रत्याशी 'इंडिया गठबंधन' और 'PDA प्रत्याशी' होगा। और दूसरी तरफ़, कांग्रेस से पूछे बिना सपा ने अपने झंडे के नीचे 5 प्रत्याशी घोषित कर दिए! कांग्रेस सिर्फ़ देखती रह गई। गठबंधन से पहले ही कांग्रेस हँसी का पात्र बन गई। और इन 5 में से 4 टिकट एक ही वोट बैंक को, दलित एक भी नहीं। नाम PDA का, काम तुष्टीकरण का। सपा बदली नहीं। याद कीजिए 2013, जब अखिलेश सरकार ने ब्लास्ट के आरोपियों पर से मुकदमे वापस लेने की कोशिश की थी, और हाईकोर्ट को रोकना पड़ा। जो अपने साथी का सम्मान नहीं रख सकते, वो उत्तर प्रदेश का सम्मान क्या रखेंगे? #UP2027
— Rajeshwar Singh (@RajeshwarS73) November 24, 2026
BJP MLA Rajeshwar Singh, a former Enforcement Directorate officer, pointed to the apparent contradiction between Akhilesh Yadav's public appeal for consensus and his party's unilateral announcement of candidates.
"Look at the difference between what they say and what they do! Honourable Akhilesh ji writes to Congress: 'Not seat-sharing, but seat adjustment', 'Candidates will not be imposed', every candidate will be an 'INDIA alliance' and 'PDA candidate'. And on the other hand, without even asking Congress, the SP has announced five candidates under its own banner! Congress could only stand by and watch," he posted on X.
The former ED joint director, who is now the MLA from Lucknow's Sarojini Nagar constituency, went on to claim that the Congress had already become a laughing stock.
"Even before the alliance, Congress had become a laughing stock. And of these five, four tickets go to the same vote bank, not a single one to Dalits. PDA in name, appeasement in practice. "Those who cannot respect their own allies - how will they respect Uttar Pradesh?" he added.
Sources close to Congress's UP working president Imran Masood suggested that the party was considering fielding a candidate against the SP in Saharanpur, a constituency won by the SP in the previous Assembly election.
The Congress has not officially reacted to the SP's candidate list, but sources said the party was deeply taken aback by the announcement.
This is not the first time the Samajwadi Party has resorted to what political analysts describe as pressure tactics. In 2024, too, the party had publicly announced candidates for constituencies where seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress were still underway.
Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit earlier this month, Akhilesh Yadav had said the Congress initially sought 181 seats. That demand came down to 131 when the two parties held their first formal round of talks on Monday. The meeting lasted just 15 minutes.
At Tuesday's meeting, the Congress further trimmed its demand, bringing its wishlist down to 110 seats. The SP, however, stuck to its offer of 26.
But the disagreement was not limited to the number of seats. Insiders said the SP also asked the Congress to share the names of its prospective candidates, a demand the Congress was unwilling to entertain.

title: Biker Dies After Chinese 'Manjha' Slits His Throat On Delhi-Mumbai Expressway
description: According to police, the banned string got entangled around his neck, causing a deep cut to his throat, because of which he lost control of his motorcycle and crashed.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
A 26-year-old man died after a stray Chinese kite string (manjha) slit his throat while he was riding a motorcycle near Barapullah on a stretch of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, police said on Tuesday.
The incident occurred when Vikas Singh was returning home from work on Monday, according to preliminary information.
According to his relatives, Singh got married around two years ago and had a three-month-old child.
According to police, the banned string got entangled around his neck, causing a deep cut to his throat, because of which he lost control of his motorcycle and crashed.
Police took the body into custody and sent it for a postmortem. Further investigation is underway.
Umesh Soni, the victim's father-in-law, said his son-in-law was returning home when the tragedy struck, leaving behind a young wife and their three-month-old child.
"I received a call from my daughter. She was distressed and told me that my son-in-law had met with an accident. I immediately rushed to the spot, where I found his body and police personnel. He was lying in a pool of blood, with severe injuries to his neck. The officers told me that his neck had got entangled in Chinese manjha and he died on the spot," Soni said.
He said the police were investigating how the banned kite string reached the expressway and demanded stringent action against those responsible for its sale and use.
Recalling the couple's life together, Soni said his daughter and son-in-law had solemnised their love marriage in court around two years ago. They had recently welcomed a child and were looking forward to building a happy life together.
"They were very happy. Their child is barely three months old. This killer string has snatched away all their happiness," he said.
The grief was palpable at the victim's home, where his wife was inconsolable. Neighbours and relatives who gathered there tried to comfort her, but she remained shattered by the sudden loss of her husband, with their infant child now left without a father.
Delhi has witnessed a series of fatal accidents and serious injuries caused by sharp kite strings, particularly banned Chinese manjha, over the past several years.
Despite restrictions on its sale and use, the dangerous string has repeatedly injured commuters, especially two-wheeler riders, by cutting into their necks and faces. Several people, including children, have lost their lives in such incidents.
The incidents have claimed several lives in the Capital.
In July 2023, a seven-year-old girl died after her throat was slit, while she was travelling on a scooter with her parents in Paschim Vihar.
In August 2024, Delhi Traffic Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Surendra Bhati, 47, and a 34-year-old businessman, Himanshu Lal, sustained serious neck injuries in separate incidents in Northeast Delhi.
On June 27, 2025, 22-year-old Yash Goswami died after Chinese manjha slit his throat while he was riding a scooter near Rani Jhansi flyover in North Delhi. The same year, another man, Prakash, suffered facial injuries near Shastri Park flyover, while 30-year-old Rajneesh died after sustaining a deep neck wound on the Sarita Vihar-Faridabad carriageway in August.
The danger persisted in 2026, when a five-year-old boy died after his throat was slit by the banned string in New Usmanpur on May 3.
On August 5, a 32-year-old businessman suffered a serious neck injury in Uttam Nagar, followed by another incident in Maujpur on August 16, in which a 35-year-old motorcyclist sustained a throat injury.
On October 11, Rakesh Kumar was injured near First Pusta on the Delhi-Dehradun highway and was rushed to hospital by traffic police personnel.
Another man, Mahesh, sustained a deep neck wound near Nehru Camp on National Highway 24 on October 20 but survived after receiving timely medical attention.

title: Bengaluru Metro Blue Line Trial Begins From KR Puram, Targets Mid-2027 Opening For Public
description: The Greater Bengaluru Development minister said the need for Metro connectivity along the Outer Ring Road was recognised as early as 2016-17.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
Trial runs on the Phase 2A section of the Blue Line Metro corridor along Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road commenced from KR Puram on Tuesday, with public operations targeted for mid-2027, Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said.
The trials began at the first four stations towards Mahadevapura and will progressively extend to other stations in the coming weeks, he said after inspecting the progress of work at Doddanekkundi Metro Station.
Gowda described the Blue Line as a critical infrastructure project for Bengaluru, particularly for the Outer Ring Road (ORR), which has emerged as one of the city's major employment and mobility corridors.
"An estimated 11-12 lakh people work along this stretch. The corridor is vital not only for the daily commute of thousands of employees but also for Bengaluru's economic activity and the wider growth of Karnataka and the country. The Metro is expected to provide a long-term public transport solution to the severe congestion commuters face along this stretch," he said.
Here is your first look at the Blue Line of Namma Metro - the next major addition to our comprehensive set of solutions to mobility challenges in BLR. We have reached a milestone - trial runs have started on this section. From KR Pura the train is now running up to Doddenakundi. Automated signalling will be operationalised in a couple of months. Then we are ready for safety certification. We are actively pushing at every stage for early dedication to public use.
— Krishna Byre Gowda (@krishnabgowda) November 24, 2026
The Greater Bengaluru Development minister said the need for Metro connectivity along the Outer Ring Road was recognised as early as 2016-17, when the planning process for Phases 2A and 2B began.
The projects received State Cabinet approval in 2017, following which proposals were submitted to the Union Government. Construction began in 2020, he said.
According to a statement, the 19-km Phase 2A corridor, extending from KR Puram to Central Silk Board, comprises 13 stations.
Trial runs have commenced from KR Puram across the first four stations, with testing scheduled to continue through this month.
The trials are expected to be extended to another four stations next month.
Gowda said installation of the automatic signalling system was pending and was expected to be completed over the next two to three months, following which the mandatory safety certification process would begin.
He said the government was working towards completing the signalling installation by January and commencing safety certification after February.
Considering the testing and certification requirements, the entire process was expected to take another seven to eight months, with the corridor targeted to open for public operations by mid-2027, he said.
The minister said the government had directed officials to expedite work on Phase 2B by coordinating closely with contractors, particularly along the KR Puram-Hebbal stretch, where construction progress needed to be improved.
The entire Blue Line project, spanning 58.2 km from Central Silk Board through KR Puram and Hebbal to Kempegowda International Airport, is being implemented at an estimated cost of around Rs 20,000 crore, officials said.
The government is targeting completion of the entire corridor within the next one-and-a-half years, they added.
On the financial challenges associated with Metro expansion, Gowda said the State Government was ensuring that funding constraints did not hamper ongoing projects.
The State bears the burden of loan repayments and also provides financial assistance to meet the operating losses of the Metro corporation, he said.
He pointed out that foreign exchange fluctuations had increased the repayment burden, with the dollar rising from around Rs 70-80 at the time of borrowing to approximately Rs 100 now, adding nearly 30 per cent to the loan burden.
Delays in project approvals had also contributed to an increase in the cost of construction materials and overall project expenditure, he alleged.
"Despite these pressures, the government has made budgetary provisions and is releasing funds as required to ensure that projects do not face delays due to a shortage of money," he said.
Gowda said the state government had held discussions with the union government on its proposal for the Red Line Metro expansion.
He said the state was yet to receive final approval, nearly 22 months after the Chief Minister (D K Shivakumar) and he submitted a request to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
"A recent meeting with Central Government officials in Delhi saw the State's proposal discussed constructively, although no final decision was taken," he added.
The state has also submitted a proposal to the Centre for a double-decker corridor from Sarjapur through Ibbalur Junction to St John's, officials said.
With residential and commercial development along Sarjapur Road gathering pace and traffic volumes increasing, the proposal seeks to address future mobility requirements through integrated Metro and road infrastructure, they added.
The minister said the government was also examining ways to strengthen the Metro corporation's revenue streams and improve its financial self-sufficiency.
Ticket revenue was currently insufficient to meet the corporation's entire operating expenditure. Including depreciation, the corporation records an annual loss of around Rs 600-700 crore, although it is estimated to be in an operating surplus of Rs 50-60 crore when depreciation is excluded, he said.
The commencement of Blue Line operations was also expected to increase operating expenditure, he added.
Gowda said the objective was to build a financially sustainable Metro system that could meet its day-to-day operational requirements without depending entirely on government grants.
However, he sought to clarify that no decision had been taken on increasing Metro ticket fares.
Any comparison with the Delhi Metro, he said, must take into account differences in Central Government financial support, network length and passenger volumes, among other factors.

title: 2 Accused Who Robbed, Murdered Assam Family Injured In Police Encounter
description: The accused, Raju Das, who was also the tenant, was arrested along with his associate after a couple and their daughter were found dead inside their residence in Duliajan in Dibrugarh.
author: Ratnadip Choudhury
content:
Two accused in the Assam triple murder case, identified as Raju Das and Amir Das, sustained injuries in a police encounter near Balijan Tea Estate in Dibrugarh district on Wednesday morning.
According to preliminary information, the accused allegedly tried to escape from a police vehicle while being transported by the investigating team. Police opened fire when the duo attempted to flee, leaving both with bullet injuries. Two police personnel were also injured in the incident.
The two accused and the injured policemen have been taken to Duliajan Oil Hospital for treatment, and their medical condition is not immediately known.
Raju and Amir are accused of killing three members of a family at their residence in Kamalabari area of Assam's Duliajan.
The victims were identified as retired Oil India Limited employee Chandrakanta Bhuyan, his wife Eliza Bhuyan and their daughter Niharika Bhuyan. Their bodies were recovered from the house after neighbours raised an alarm when the family members failed to respond on November 16.
Raju and Amir were arrested a day later from Simaluguri Railway Station in Assam's Sivasagar district. The two were intercepted while travelling on the Avadh Assam Express. Investigators suspected that the accused were attempting to reach Guwahati before fleeing to Bengaluru.
During the investigation, police found that Raju had allegedly lost around Rs 4 lakh in online gaming and betting and was facing financial difficulties. He had reportedly borrowed money from his father. Investigators suspected that the robbery was planned to recover the money.
Raju had worked as a caretaker for the Bhuyan family for several years and was familiar with their residence and daily routine. Police said that the three family members were attacked with a hammer and an iron rod before cash, gold ornaments and other valuables were taken from the house.
Police subsequently recovered several items suspected to have been stolen from the residence, including gold and silver ornaments, cash and mobile phones.
As part of the investigation, the accused were also taken to the crime scene for reconstruction in the presence of a magistrate and senior police officials. Dummy bodies were used during the exercise to recreate the sequence of events.
Investigators also searched a hotel in Assam's Tinsukia district while looking for a woman suspected of assisting the accused after the murders. Police were examining her alleged role in helping the duo evade arrest.
Raju had earlier been arrested in a kidnapping case in 2020 and had spent around three months in jail before securing bail.

title: Miranda House Offers 15 Certificate Courses In AI, Filmmaking, Animation
description: The AI filmmaking course will train students in AI-enabled content creation, while the influencer and creator business programme will prepare them for the commercial and professional aspects of the creator economy.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
Miranda House, University of Delhi, is offering 15 professional certificate courses in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and Eros AIVidya. The six-month programmes will provide industry-oriented training in emerging creative and digital fields, equipping students with skills in artificial intelligence (AI), filmmaking, animation, virtual reality, and the creator economy.
Admissions will be based on merit and are open to eligible University of Delhi students.
The courses cover areas such as AI filmmaking, influencer and creator business, avatar and digital human creation, animation, video blogging, augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) production, visual effects (VFX), scriptwriting, acting, music production, music composition and direction, sound editing, video editing and art direction.
The AI filmmaking course will train students in AI-enabled content creation, while the influencer and creator business programme will prepare them for the commercial and professional aspects of the creator economy.
Other courses will focus on developing students' skills in animation, acting, scriptwriting, music production, sound editing, video editing and visual effects.
Under the partnership, 15 top-performing students who demonstrate excellence during the programmes will receive support to establish their own businesses. The initiative aims to extend opportunities beyond certification by helping students gain practical experience through creative projects and preparing them for career opportunities and entrepreneurship.
Eligibility, Fees And Admission
Students currently enrolled at the University of Delhi are eligible to apply. Admission will be based on merit, and the course fees range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1.5 lakh.
Speaking about the collaboration, Arunkumar Pillai, CEO of NSDC, said the creative economy is rapidly evolving with the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital technologies, creating demand for new capabilities and interdisciplinary talent.
"As technology continues to transform industries and create new forms of work, it is important that learners have access to relevant and future-oriented skill development opportunities. The creative economy is rapidly evolving with the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital technologies, creating demand for new capabilities and interdisciplinary talent. Through this collaboration with Eros AIVidya, we aim to support learners in acquiring industry-relevant skills that enhance employability and prepare them for emerging opportunities in the orange economy," he said.

title: Nepal PM Balen Shah's India Visit Marks New Chapter In Ties, Says Brother-In-Law
description: Sejekan said Balen Shah's rise was particularly remarkable because he had neither an established political dynasty nor traditional political backing.
author: Aditya Raj Kaul
content:
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's maiden visit to India since assuming office was more than a diplomatic milestone for his family. It was an emotional moment and, according to his brother-in-law Harish Kumar Sejekan, the beginning of a potentially transformative chapter in India-Nepal relations.
Speaking exclusively to NDTV Foreign Affairs Editor Aditya Raj Kaul after the two-day visit, Sejekan described the welcome extended to Balen Shah by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, including the ceremonial guard of honour and the warmth shared by the two leaders, as deeply moving.
Recalling watching the visuals with his wife, Sejekan said the family was overwhelmed with emotion. "We had tears in our eyes," he told NDTV, reflecting on the journey of a young man who went from nurturing political ambitions to becoming Kathmandu's mayor and eventually Nepal's Prime Minister.
Sejekan said Balen Shah's rise was particularly remarkable because he had neither an established political dynasty nor traditional political backing. His ascent, he said, was driven by hard work, conviction and a direct connection with ordinary Nepalis.
The visit comes against the backdrop of Nepal's Gen Z-led political upheaval, which reflected widespread public frustration with corruption, established political parties and governance failures. Balen Shah emerged as a symbol of political change, carrying the expectations of a generation demanding accountability and effective leadership.
His brother-in-law pointed to his tenure as Kathmandu mayor as evidence of his administrative credentials, arguing that his approach to governance and uncompromising stance on corruption helped build public confidence. He also attributed Shah's political instincts to his upbringing, highlighting the values of discipline, honesty and staying true to oneself.
Describing the Prime Minister's personality, Sejekan said conviction and fearlessness had defined him since childhood. Shah's rap music, he observed, frequently addressed social problems and issues affecting ordinary people, helping him connect with the public long before entering mainstream politics.
The India visit, he argued, demonstrated that the new leadership was focused on delivering tangible outcomes rather than diplomatic symbolism. He highlighted the railway inauguration, financial assistance, cooperation involving IITs and cricket as emerging avenues of collaboration between the two countries.
Sejekan also expressed optimism about the future of bilateral relations, identifying common priorities between Modi and Shah, particularly clean governance, development and a zero-tolerance approach towards corruption.
He recalled Shah's personal connection with India, where he had spent considerable time during his studies, particularly in Bengaluru. The Nepali leader, he said, enjoyed South Indian cuisine, music and films, while maintaining an appreciation for India's cultural diversity.
The conversation also touched upon Shah's address at the United Nations General Assembly, which attracted considerable attention. Sejekan said he continued to receive calls from people praising the speech, describing the Prime Minister's confidence on an international platform as particularly noteworthy.
Reflecting on NDTV's Anviksha Summit in Kathmandu in August, which brought together political leaders, policymakers, business representatives and cultural personalities from both countries, Sejekan offered an enthusiastic endorsement. While devastating floods in Nepal prevented him from following much of the event, he said he was delighted that NDTV had organised such an international platform in the country.
He particularly welcomed the participation of leaders across political lines, including representatives of the BJP and Congress, arguing that national interests must take precedence over partisan affiliations.
"I think at the end of the day, we should all look at our national interests first," he told Kaul, congratulating NDTV and its management for bringing diverse voices together on a common platform.
His remarks offered a glimpse into the family's perspective on a leader whose political journey has captured the imagination of Nepal's younger generation. More broadly, they reflected an expectation that the warmth generated by the Modi-Shah meeting would translate into sustained cooperation, stronger connectivity and shared prosperity for the people of India and Nepal.

title: Akhilesh Yadav's Open Letter, Then A Move That Overlaps Congress Wishlist
description: In the seat-sharing arrangement, the Congress wants a hundred seats, Samajwadi is reluctant to spare more than 26, and the gap between these two numbers tells you everything about the alliance dynamics.
author: Ranveer Singh, Jainendra Kumar, Ajay Kumar Dubey, Chandrajit Mitra
content:
The Congress-Samajwadi alliance talks for Uttar Pradesh elections appear to have hit a deadlock. Their negotiations ran through its second day without a clear deal, their wishlists overlapped, and now, sources suggest, friendly fight is possible in at least one seat.
In an effort to break the deadlock, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has reached out to its evergreen ally through an open letter. Calling the upcoming elections a "historic opportunity" to dethrone the BJP, Yadav has called for "serious talks", taking public expectations and realities into account.
"We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our 'alliance' wins in most constituencies. Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he said in an X post.
READ | Samajwadi Party Unveils First List For 5 Seats For UP Polls. Congress Sought 2 Of Those
The Congress is understood to have sought at least a hundred seats from its rather dominating ally in the heartland state. There are a total 403 seats in UP, but the Samajwadi Party appears far from ready to spare one-fourth of that to the Congress. In contrast to their demand, Samajwadi has offered 26 seats to the Congress, though Yadav appeared to be a little more considerate.
"In addition to the 26 seats from the priority list your team provided that we have discussed today, please identify and send us all other potential seats. Then we will sit down together and assess which seats, and which candidates for those seats, are in a winning position. Based on our assessment and the mathematical equation for victory, we may also be able to tell the Congress about many winnable seats it has not even considered for some reason," the Samajwadi chief has said.
Caste arithmetic being central to elections in heartland states, both Congress and its ally are banking on who they suggest are the oppressed lot. Yadav's party calls them the PDA, or Pichra (backward classes), Dalit, Alpasankhyak (minorities).
Yadav credited this vote bank for their performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections that saw a massive drop in the BJP's seat count, and a rise in that of the opposition's INDIA alliance.
Differences over seat-sharing, Yadav is aware, could make it awkward for both, dilute a joint arsenal and pit them against their own allies - and this may end up helping the BJP.
Yadav offered a plan to avoid that: "The truth is that we do not want the seats divided on an 'us-versus-you' basis. We would rather call it not a division, but a 'seat adjustment'. In constituencies with difficult electoral equations, we will discuss at least two candidates together, choose the one with the better chance of winning, and work together to get them elected. We do not want candidates to be imposed on one another within the alliance; they should be decided by consensus. Only then will your votes and ours transfer to one another, ensuring our victory, and tomorrow we will be able to say together what we have already said."
READ | Congress Wants 100 Seats In UP. Samajwadi Party Offers 26, Cites Past Results
"This is not about seats, but about victory," he added, but then came a surprise.
When Wishes Overlap
The UP scenario is much like two brothers having their eyes on the same last piece of toy left on the shelf, and one of them declares loudly he's having it.
Samajwadi Party did exactly that. It unveiled its candidates for five seats in UP today: Behat, Saharanpur, Shamli, Amroha, and Lalitpur. Sources close to the Congress suggest that of these five, Behat and Saharanpur were on Congress' wishlist too. Both had been won by the Samajwadi Party in 2022.
This isn't the first time Samajwadi has employed what analysts point to as 'pressure tactics'. Back in 2024 too, the party had publicly declared candidates for seats that were still under discussion.
Friendly Fire In INDIA Camp?
The worst fear in the breakdown in the alliance talks is a friendly fight that could have easily been avoided. It threatens to split votes, and a small swing could risk giving away the fight to another party.
Buzz coming out of the Congress camp appears to hint at a similar scenario.
Sources close to Congress's UP working president Imran Masood suggested that the party plans to field candidates against the Samajwadi Party in Saharanpur - one that had been won by the SP last time. There has been no Congress response to the SP's candidates list, but sources said that the party was well taken aback.
READ | List Of 130, Then Tea: Congress Gets 'Can't Take Risk' Reply From Samajwadi Party
Congress-SP Talks
The developments played out over the day after the Congress and SP met for the second round of seat-sharing talks, which began yesterday.
Initially, the Congress had a wishlist of 181 seats, Akhilesh Yadav had claimed while speaking at HT Leadership Summit earlier this month. That came down to 131 when the leaders met yesterday for the first formal talks. The meeting lasted 15 minutes.
In today's meeting, the Congress gave another trim to its wishlist, and now it has 110 names. The SP offered 26. But that wasn't the only difference. Insiders said that during the meeting, the Samajwadi asked Congress not only for seats but also for the names of candidates, for which the Congress was not ready.
According to sources, Samajwadi MP Rajiv Rai also advised the Congress not to repeat its "Bihar mistake" that saw the party being decimated. In a sarcastic response, Imran Masood is understood to have replied, 'We are zero and whoever we chase will multiply tenfold.'
This meeting went on for three and a half hours, but there appeared no headway. A third round of talks would be held after two days, leaders from the two parties said.
The seat-sharing would be finalised over the next two meetings, they hoped.

title: Amid Deepam Row, Thiruparankundram Temple Says It Stood By Tradition
description: The ceremonial lamp was lit at 6 pm at its traditional location at Uchipillayar Deepa Mandapam atop a Thirupparankundram hillock in conformity with a unanimous resolution to uphold established worship practices, the Board said.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
Hours after lighting the Karthigai Deepam only at the customary location atop the Thiruparankundram hill and skipping the court-directed stone pillar, the temple's Board of Trustees asserted that long-standing religious traditions must take precedence.
The ceremonial lamp was lit at 6 pm at its traditional location at Uchipillayar Deepa Mandapam atop a Thiruparankundram hillock in conformity with a unanimous resolution to uphold established worship practices, the Board said.
In a statement, chairman of the Board of Trustees, V Shanmugasundaram, defended the decision to not light the lamp at the stone pillar. He said that the rituals were governed by "Agama" rules which form the core of the religious practices of the shrine and it must be protected.
Underscoring the historical continuity of festivals and prayers at the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy temple, the Board said that the Karthigai Deepam festival was performed according to traditions. The trustees added that these foundational customs need to be formally placed before the Supreme Court for its consideration.
Explaining the significance of the customary venue, the board highlighted that the lamp is traditionally lit only at the "Deepa Mandapam" near the Uchipillayar Temple because of its sacred alignment; it is directly above the main presiding deity (Moolavar Lord Subramaniya Swamy).

title: Japanese Woman's First Overnight Train Journey In India Goes Viral, Internet Reacts
description: While she praised the comfort and safety of the journey, she complained about the freezing temperatures inside the train. Her post has sparked a lively discussion online.
author: Nikhil Pandey
content:
A Japanese Instagrammer named Miyu has shared her experience of travelling on an overnight train in India, and her post has attracted considerable attention on social media. Her 14-hour journey from Udaipur to Agra in an air-conditioned 3-tier (3AC) coach has received around 40,000 views and prompted several comments from users.
Sharing a glimpse of the journey on Instagram, Miyu described it as a bucket-list experience. She said she had never woken up quite like this before, adding that the experience had left her wide awake.
Despite the unusual wake-up experience, Miyu appeared pleased with the journey. She described the 3AC coach as comfortable and safe, although she had one major complaint: it was extremely cold inside the train.
Watch the video here:
Social media users share mixed reactions
The video prompted a range of responses, with users sharing their own experiences of Indian train travel and offering suggestions for places Miyu could visit during her stay.
One user jokingly commented on the challenges of finding a place to stand on a crowded Indian train, saying, "I wonder if it was really fun. When I stand in a place like this, I feel there is no empty seat. I also wonder whether an auto or a relative's bike will be waiting for me when I get off the train."
Another user welcomed Miyu to India and suggested exploring Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur for their palaces and history. The user also recommended visiting the mountains and historic forts of Maharashtra.
"Hope you enjoyed a lot. India is a great and diverse country in terms of landscape," another comment read.
However, some users also offered safety advice. One person warned Miyu against enjoying the journey by standing near the train door, calling it dangerous.
Another user suggested visiting Mathura and Vrindavan, which are close to Agra, and recommended Prem Mandir in Vrindavan. The commenter described the white marble temple as a place where visitors can experience stories from Lord Krishna's childhood.
A glimpse into India's train travel experience
Indian Railways connects cities across the country through an extensive network of trains, offering travellers different classes of accommodation. The 3AC category provides air-conditioned accommodation with sleeping berths and is a popular option for overnight journeys.
Miyu's post offers a glimpse into the experience of travelling across India by train, while the comments reflect the varied experiences and advice of people familiar with the country's railway network.

title: Pregnant Woman, 19, Beaten, Poisoned And Smothered To Death By Parents In Iran Honour Killing Case
description: A 19-year-old pregnant woman in Iran was allegedly killed by her parents in an honour killing case.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
A 19-year-old pregnant woman has been brutally murdered in Iran in what is being dubbed a case of honour killing. The victim, identified as Helia Fattahi, was two months pregnant following a relationship with a young man when she disclosed the news to her family last week. The enraged parents then allegedly forced her to swallow approximately 30 anticonvulsant pills and severely beat her before suffocating her to death with a pillow.
The incident took place in the western Iranian city of Sanandaj, and the accused parents, Voria Fattahi and Leila Veis, have been arrested by the authorities on charges of killing their daughter, according to a report in Iran International. Both the parents confessed to the killing during interrogation.
The parents initially went to court on Saturday (Nov 21) to file a complaint against Fattahi. Upon returning, they forced her to swallow the pills. However, after realising she was still alive, they used a pillow to suffocate her to death, as per Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights.
Hengaw and another human rights group, Hana, described the murder as a so-called 'honour' killing.
"The Islamic Republic of Iran's failure to enact effective laws protecting women and children from domestic violence, together with legal loopholes and lenient penalties for perpetrators of so-called “honour killings,” leaves women vulnerable to structural violence and reinforces a culture of impunity," Hengaw said.
Fate Of Females In Iran
The incident has once again triggered a conversation about the persecution of women in Iran. Fattahi's death is the third killing of a young woman in Iran in a little over a week. Last Wednesday (Nov 18), 23-year-old Sadaf Haghbin was shot dead at her birthday party in Gilan province by an ex-boyfriend after she refused to marry him.
Prior to that, Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old schoolgirl in Kermanshah, died after falling from the fifth floor of a building. A national network of teachers' unions said she had warned school staff that her father would kill her if they sent her home with him.
Earlier this week, Iranian authorities lashed a prominent singer and four members of her team 74 times after a performance was viewed millions of times on YouTube.
Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, was sentenced in June to the lashes along with four musicians and four members of her crew for the concert posted online in December 2024. The performance featured Ahmadi singing powerful, mournful songs to an empty audience on a dimly lit stage adorned solely with a large Persian carpet.

title: British Couple Expresses Sadness Leaving 'Pretty Special' Goa: 'It's Making Me Emotional'
description: UK family shares sadness leaving Goa after a week at Palolem Beach, describing it as their ideal place.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
A UK couple travelling the globe with their children said they were feeling 'bloody sad' leaving 'pretty special' Goa after a week at Palolem Beach. In a now-viral clip, Aimee Bedford, 39, and Lee Bodell, 47, who left Birkenhead, Merseyside, in July this year, said Goa embodied everything they wanted and mirrored their ideal life.
Visibly emotional about the impending farewell, Aimee said she would carry Goa's "people, culture, friendships, sunsets, and experiences" with her long after she left.
"I have just come on to share how bloody sad I am about leaving Goa tomorrow. So yeah, we have been here for a week, and I cannot tell you how amazing it's been," said Aimee.
"It's just been beautiful because it aligns with everything we're trying to achieve longer term in terms of what our life is gonna look like, and it will look like it," she added/
The traveller said there was something about Goa that made her feel at home almost instantly. She added that the coastal Indian state was very welcoming and inclusive to her family.
"It has just been incredible, and I think for me what's making me emotional is that the children have learned so much. They've seen so much in seven days and it's a very special place, and one that I don't wanna leave. But we have to. I think that's the hardest part of travelling is that you find places that you wanna stay longer. Sometimes you can, but this time we can't," she said.
Check The Clip Here:

title: After GTA 6 Success, Rockstar Games Willing To Sell Red Dead Redemption Film, TV Rights For $100 Million
description: Rockstar and Take-Two consider licensing Red Dead Redemption rights for a $100 million film or TV adaptation.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
Following the monstrous success of Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), Rockstar Games is now turning its attention towards its other crown jewel, the Red Dead Redemption (RDR) universe. The developer and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, are reportedly considering a film or television adaptation of the hit Western action franchise. To make this happen, the studio is allegedly willing to license the adaptation rights for $100 million, as per a report in The Ankler.
With GTA 6 earning close to $4 billion in pre-sales alone, dwarfing the entire theatrical box office runs of prominent movies like Avengers: Endgame and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, it is clear that Hollywood needs gaming's biggest franchises more than gaming needs Hollywood.
If any studio is able to gain access to the RDR universe at the reported fee, it will still be a bargain, as Amazon paid $250 million in 2017 for the global television rights to The Lord of the Rings.
The Western action series kicked off 22 years ago with Red Dead Revolver before truly finding its footing with Red Dead Redemption in 2010. However, it was the 2018 release of Red Dead Redemption 2 that cemented Rockstar as one of the biggest gaming studios on the planet, boasting gameplay that revolutionised the industry. To this day, RDR 2 remains the third-best-selling game of all time, with its groundbreaking mechanics paving the way for GTA 6.
Also Read | 'Cyberpunk 2 Is Cancelled': CD Projekt Red Developer After GTA 6 Success
'We're Very Selective'
Despite having an enviable roster of successful IPs, Rockstar and Take-Two have been rather conservative when it comes to allowing their games to be adapted for other mediums. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said the company was 'very, very selective' regarding the matter but acknowledged that they would be open to the idea if the creatives were passionate.
“We're very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment we're always proud of. We would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it," Zelnick told Variety.
"If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that. And of course, there's always a risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective.”
If the project is greenlit, it could reach similar or greater heights as Bethesda's Fallout and Naughty Dog's The Last of Us, both of which have become some of the biggest shows in recent years on Prime Video and HBO.

title: Australian Woman Gives Hyderabad Metro 10/10 After First Ride In India
description: While she praised its cleanliness, comfort and ease of travel, her viral video has sparked a debate over the experience during peak hours.
author: Nikhil Pandey
content:
An Australian woman living in Melbourne has praised Hyderabad Metro after travelling on it for the first time during a visit to India with her Indian husband and son. Her video sharing the experience has gone viral on social media.
Crystal described the journey in three words, saying she had not expected such a positive experience.
'A stress-free experience'
In the video, Crystal said she had never travelled by train in India before and wanted to see how it compared with trains in Australia.
She said she was impressed by the station's cleanliness as soon as she entered. The train was equally clean, she added, pointing out that it also had a separate coach for women to make their journeys more comfortable.
Crystal also praised the temperature inside the train, saying it was just right.
"Overall, it was a stress-free experience," she said.
'I travelled during off-peak hours'
Describing the journey, Crystal said the metro was fast, spotless and very easy to use. She added that she thoroughly enjoyed the experience and gave Hyderabad Metro a perfect score of 10 out of 10.
However, she acknowledged that her experience might have been different had she travelled during peak hours, when trains are likely to be more crowded.
"I did not expect such a good experience," she said, adding that people travelling during busy hours might have a different experience.
Social media users debate peak-hour experience
The video, shared on Instagram, has sparked a discussion about travelling on Hyderabad Metro during peak hours.
While some users said the overall experience remained good despite the crowds, others argued that travelling during rush hour could be uncomfortable.
One user commented, "Travelling on Hyderabad Metro is fine as long as it is not extremely crowded."
Another wrote, "I do not care about peak hours. I just love avoiding traffic. However, you need to navigate the crowds at Ameerpet when travelling towards Raidurg."
A third user advised Crystal to avoid travelling during busy hours, adding that even the women's coach could become overcrowded.
Another user questioned the criticism of Hyderabad Metro during peak hours, saying that overcrowding was common on metro systems in every major city.
"Just a reminder, Hyderabad Metro is much better than the NYC Metro," the user added.

title: After Ensuring His Nvidia Comeback, Trump Says He May Pardon Jensen Huang
description: Trump also said he has thought about having the US government take a stake in Nvidia, saying, "It's probably not too late."
author: Sanstuti Nath
content:
President Donald Trump has reportedly said a pardon for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for any potential crimes was "always an option", but he added that the extreme step is likely won't be needed. The president, who has taken credit for Huang's entry to Nvidia, urged the billionaire executive to "tell the truth" when he testifies before Congress next week.
"It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," Trump said during an interview with the New York Post when asked about pardoning Huang.
"I don't think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it's an interesting story for people...I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I've always found him to be 100 per cent aboveboard, and you know, a very smart person," he added.
Trump also said he has thought about having the US government take a stake in Nvidia, saying, "It's probably not too late."
The US leader's comments come a day after Nvidia's board brought Huang--one of the most prominent figures in the artificial intelligence industry-- back as CEO in a stunning reversal after Trump himself intervened in the matter.
During the interview, Trump also expressed his satisfaction with how the market responded after Hunag's return to Nvidia, with the chipmaker's stock rising more than 30 per cent, and pointed out that the stock had recovered.
"That's not bad, went down a couple of points," Trump said. "It really picked up at the end."
Nvidia Remains Under Scrutiny
Nvidia board's stunning reversal to bring back Huang has spurred questions about its independence and what Trump's role means for the meeting of business and politics.
"To bow to pressure to bring someone back who has hurt the reputation of the company is crazy," Kathleen Day, a lecturer at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School, told the Associated Press.
Nvidia's board includes both business leaders with longstanding ties to the company and a group of more recent additions who have experience at big-name companies including Taco Bell, PepsiCo and Eli Lilly. Some experts have called for the board to resign in the wake of the havoc.
Meanwhile, Huang is scheduled for a closed-door meeting on Tuesday with the House Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence committees on topics including his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy, and his company's security protocols.
He is set to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday.

title: AI Consumes Less Water Per Dollar Spent Than Almond Milk Or Golf: Report
description: The report puts $25 a month of AI spending at about 1.9 gallons of water consumption. According to the report, $25 spent on almond milk consumes 308 gallons of water, while the same amount spent on golf course green fees consumes 679 gallons.
author: Reuters
content:
Artificial intelligence consumes less water per dollar spent than almond milk or golf, according to a new study from Enverus Intelligence Research.
The report puts $25 a month of AI spending at about 1.9 gallons of water consumption, including water used to generate the electricity that powers data centers.
According to the report, $25 spent on almond milk consumes 308 gallons of water, while the same amount spent on golf course green fees consumes 679 gallons
Household electricity on an all-natural-gas grid consumes about 31 gallons for the same spending, says the report
Enverus' report, "Data Center Water Use | Setting the Record Straight," compares water consumption using a consistent monthly spending benchmark
"If a typical consumer is worried about their water footprint, skipping one almond latte a week does more than giving up AI chatbots entirely," said Ryan Luther, director of Energy Transition Research at the firm
About 90% of the water attributed to running AI models is consumed at power plants rather than data centers, the report found
Enverus said a modern hyperscale data center campus consumes about 32,100 gallons of water per acre per month, less than rice, almonds or alfalfa, and similar to an average US golf course.

title: Trump Pardons Turkeys 'Freedom And Feathers' From Fowl Thanksgiving Fate
description: Trump granted pardons to Freedom and Feathers, the 4-month-old fowl selected for the annual White House ritual.
author: Reuters
content:
US President Donald Trump has described the presidential pardon as "extreme powers." On Tuesday, he used it to spare two turkeys from the imminent threat of becoming Thanksgiving dinner.
Trump granted pardons to Freedom and Feathers, the 4-month-old fowl selected for the annual White House ritual.
Raised at Deans Gap Farm in Fort Seybert, West Virginia, the birds spent Monday night at the lavish Willard InterContinental Hotel in Washington before their White House appearance. Trump said next year's turkeys could stay overnight in the new White House state ballroom, where he said he would also hold the pardon ceremony.
Online voters selected Freedom to receive Trump's formal pardon, but both birds will retire to Texas A&M University after their reprieve.
At Tuesday's ceremony on the White House's new South Lawn helipad, Trump gazed at Freedom and noticed his companion was missing.
"Where's Feathers?" he asked.
The second turkey was resting in the White House, officials said. Trump quipped that he'd run off into the bushes.
Moments later, he rested his hand on the bird's fluffy white plumes.
"Freedom," Trump said, "I just want to say, that you and Feathers, as of this moment, have a complete and total pardon."
The tradition dates back more than a century, when poultry farmers sent turkeys to the White House as holiday gifts, forcing presidents and first ladies to coordinate avian logistics to handle the incoming birds - many of which arrived alive. In 1989, President George H.W. Bush formalized a reprieve for the birds, turning the annual turkey presentation into a pardon.
The rising cost of a Thanksgiving dinner could cast a shadow this year on Americans' turkey-centered feasts.
Holiday staples are 6% more expensive this year than 2025, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation. Turkey prices jumped more than 10%, according to the federation, which cited Department of Agriculture data on strong demand, including for exports, and low inventories.
Consumer prices for other Thanksgiving staples and ingredients, such as ham, milk, dinner rolls, sweet potatoes and cranberries, also increased.
Earlier on Tuesday, Trump awarded the Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, to Rudy Giuliani, his one-time personal attorney and New York mayor during the September 11, 2001, attacks on the World Trade Center buildings.
Giuliani himself was once the beneficiary of a Trump reprieve. Trump pardoned Giuliani in 2025 as he faced legal fallout for attempting to overturn the 2020 election results.
