Trump also said he was open to granting Huang a presidential pardon if necessary, but did not think such a step would be required.
Asked in an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday whether he would consider pardoning Huang over potential crimes, Trump said, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”
“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump said, adding that he wanted Huang to “just tell the truth”.
Trump said he had always found Huang to be “100% aboveboard” and described him as a “very smart person”, while acknowledging that the Nvidia chief’s lawyers would have to advise him on how to approach the questioning.
What is the Fifth Amendment?
The Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution protects individuals from being compelled to give testimony that could incriminate them in a criminal case.
The protection is commonly known as the right against self-incrimination. 
When a person refuses to answer a question on this basis, the act is often described as “pleading the Fifth”.
The amendment forms part of the Bill of Rights, ratified in 1791, and also includes protections against double jeopardy, guarantees of due process and limits on the government’s power to take private property without just compensation.
Invoking the Fifth Amendment is a constitutional right and does not, by itself, establish guilt, but it does create a sense of doubt surrounding the innocence. Whether Huang chooses to invoke it during congressional questioning would be a decision made with advice from his lawyers.
Why is Jensen Huang facing scrutiny?
Huang is expected to testify before US lawmakers in relation to questions about Nvidia’s business dealings with China and compliance with American export restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips.
The scrutiny has also centred on Huang’s relationship with a Chinese woman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence. Huang has acknowledged having an affair with the woman.
Lawmakers are also expected to examine allegations that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to Chinese AI companies through third countries, potentially circumventing US export controls.
According to CNN, Huang is scheduled to testify behind closed doors before a US Senate committee on Tuesday next week, followed by a public hearing on Friday.
The hearings are expected to focus on Nvidia’s export practices and the national security implications of its business dealings with China.
Nvidia’s board has also reinstated Huang as chief executive, following his removal from the position less than two weeks earlier. Trump had claimed credit for persuading the board to bring Huang back.

title: 'Will take Bangladesh by December 16': Bengal minister Arjun Singh vows revenge for killings of Hindus
description: NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
Bengal minister vows to avenge killings of Hindus in neighbouring Bangladesh
NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country would be "avenged", triggering fresh attention amid strained relations between the two countries.Speaking to reporters in Bhatpara on Tuesday, Singh made the remarks while referring to the killings of Hindus in Bangladesh. "We will take Bangladesh by December 16th. Enough is enough; there are no more excuses regarding Bangladesh. We will certainly take revenge for the way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh; there is no doubt about that," he said.
His remarks came amid heightened tensions in Bangladesh over the proposed return of former Prime Minister and Awami League supremo Sheikh Hasina from India. Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kobir has said that Hasina would only be allowed to return as a "prisoner, in handcuffs" and under strict surveillance.Kobir reportedly made the remarks while speaking to journalists after briefing foreign diplomats at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka.Dismissing reports that Hasina intended to return to Bangladesh on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations, he said, "Desire and reality are two different things.""The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition...
She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," Kobir said.Earlier, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali had told Reuters that the former prime minister intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.In an official communication, Ali said Hasina had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration for her return journey. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters.Meanwhile, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam reportedly dismissed Hasina's demand for a state aircraft to facilitate her return, describing it as "nothing but madness".A Bangladeshi minister had also told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would face immediate arrest and imprisonment if she returned to the country. The minister added that no formal discussions had taken place with India over arranging an aircraft for her journey.
Hasina served as Bangladesh's prime minister from 2009 until 2024. She fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a student-led agitation over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her Awami League government.She was subsequently sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal in a case involving crimes against humanity over the crackdown on protesters. Hasina has denied the allegations.Hasina first expressed her intention to return to Bangladesh during a virtual media briefing in August this year and reiterated the plan in several subsequent interviews.Earlier this month, she also applied for a fresh passport and national identity card through her legal representatives in the United Kingdom.Dhaka has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that the request is under examination.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: ‘Hardest meeting of my life’: Jensen Huang apologises to Nvidia staff after CEO comeback
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct and admitted making “very serious personal
author: Vijaya Srivastava
content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct and admitted making “very serious personal mistakes” during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the top post. Huang acknowledged that his personal behaviour had hurt his family and wife. He also promised to hold himself to higher standards and undergo regular performance reviews based on feedback from employees.
“This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang said, according to a report by The Wired. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”
Huang says he is undergoing therapy
Addressing employees, Huang said he had been attending therapy sessions every day for an hour and a half. He added that the sessions had been helping him.
“I made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife,” he said.
Huang also stressed that Nvidia's code of conduct remained applicable to everyone in the company, including its top leadership. He said he had written much of the code himself and that it was designed to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”
He warned that violations would not be tolerated. However, he clarified that every violation would not automatically lead to an employee's dismissal.
“But that does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would determine the action taken.
Nvidia CEO promises regular performance reviews
Huang also addressed criticism of his intense management style and acknowledged that his behaviour had sometimes affected employees negatively.
While he maintained that his demanding approach helped push people to perform better, he admitted that he sometimes went too far.
“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said.
He said he needed to find a way to maintain his commitment to Nvidia without hurting the people working for him.
“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” he said.
Huang also announced that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review. The process would involve seeking feedback from people working with him, potentially as often as once a month.
He said he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and did not intend to introduce the practice across the company.
Huang rejects claims of preferential treatment
The CEO also pushed back against suggestions that he had been reinstated because of his standing in the technology industry.
“There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said.
He rejected the suggestion that his position gave him special treatment or placed him above Nvidia's code of conduct.
Huang also sought to reassure women employees, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women”.
He highlighted the company's flexible work policies, saying they allowed employees to build their families while pursuing their careers.
“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” he said.
He further sought to reassure employees about the company's ability to function without him, saying his brief absence had demonstrated its operational strength.
“I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang said.
Why Huang stepped down and returned as Nvidia CEO
Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation earlier this month following concerns about his personal conduct and lack of candour. The development came after media reports about alleged extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman accused of having links to Chinese intelligence services.
However, the same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days after accepting his resignation. The decision followed fresh assurances from Huang and information from the Trump administration that he was not under federal scrutiny.
His return has drawn mixed reactions within Nvidia. While some employees welcomed the decision, others reportedly remain concerned about his conduct and the board's move to reinstate him.
The controversy has also led to continued legal and regulatory scrutiny. Nvidia's board is investigating whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. US lawmakers are also expecting him to testify before Congress next week.
Meanwhile, lawsuits and other investigations are ongoing into the company's disclosures about Huang's conduct and its compliance with US export controls on chips.

title: Delhi woman gangraped by colleagues at Preet Vihar cafe after late-night party; 3 held
description: NEW DELHI: Three people, including two women, have been arrested in connection with the alleged gang rape of a woman in Delhi’s Preet Vihar area.
author: TNN
content:
NEW DELHI: Three people, including two women, have been arrested in connection with the alleged gang rape of a woman in Delhi’s Preet Vihar area.
According to the police, the 22-year-old survivor, who reportedly works at a cafe in Karkardooma, knew all the accused and had accompanied them to a party.
On the night of the incident, all eight people went to a cafe in Preet Vihar. The cafe usually closed at 11.30 pm Monday, but one of the group members had a key and allegedly unlocked the premises to organise a late-night party.
The group allegedly consumed alcohol at the cafe and left around 3.30 am. A short while later, the woman alleged that two men had sexually assaulted her, while the other members of the group had supported them.

title: Report claims Elon Musk made $500,000 donation to Austin to help homeless young adults find homes; Tesla CEO responds
description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has confirmed reports that the Musk Foundation contributed $500,000 to a City of Austin initiative which is aimed at helping homeless
author: TOI Tech Desk
content:
Tesla CEO 
Elon Musk
 has confirmed reports that the Musk Foundation contributed $500,000 to a City of Austin initiative which is aimed at helping homeless young adults who have aged out of the foster care system secure housing and support services. This development came after a widely shared post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) highlighted the contribution, claiming that Musk had donated $500,000 to help homeless young adults so that they can find homes in Austin. Responding to the post Musk wrote ‘This news is accurate’, publicly confirming the report.
Austin secures matching funds from Musk Foundation
As per the announcement from the City of Austin, the city revealed that it has secured $500,000 in matching funds from the Musk Foundation, unlocking an additional $500,000 in city funding and bringing the total investment to $1 million. The funding is said to help as many as 100 young adults access housing assistance and supportive services as they transition from foster care to independent living.
The city officials also claimed that the young adults leaving foster care often face some really hard challenges when it comes to securing housing because they may lack the financial resources and family support networks available to many of their peers. 
The new funding by the Musk Foundation is intended to address those barriers and offer pathways to long-term stability.
Programme focused on former foster youth
Earlier this year, City Council Member Ryan Alter, who represents District 5, secured $500,000 in the city’s 2026-27 budget for housing help for former foster youth. The money was contingent on the city finding $500,000 in matching funds. With the Musk Foundation’s contribution, the full $1 million can now proceed.
“Every young person deserves a strong foundation,” said David Gray, director of Austin Homeless Strategies and Operations, saying the investment gives 100 young adults a meaningful housing opportunity. Mayor Kirk Watson said the investment supports his Generation ATX initiative, which aims to expand opportunities for the city’s next generation. Alter said the funds will help young people sleep out of extreme heat, cold or rain, and will save taxpayers from supporting them for decades.
Elon Musk weighs in
The donation attracted attention on social media after an X user highlighted the city announcement and praised the contribution. Musk later responded to the post, stating, “This news is accurate,” confirming that the reported donation had indeed been made.
The contribution comes as Austin continues to expand housing assistance programmes for former foster youth, with officials saying the combined public-private investment will help more young adults secure stable housing and access wraparound support services.

title: Israel govt formation: Eisenkot, Lieberman seal first coalition pact as rivals step up push to oust Netanyahu
description: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing opposition party on Tuesday,
author: Pranjal Pandey
content:
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing opposition party on Tuesday, marking the first such alliance since last month's election.
Yashar said Eisenkot met Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and the two agreed on a deal following their discussions, Reuters reported.
Efforts to form a government without Prime Minister 
Benjamin Netanyahu
 are gathering pace.
The Knesset was sworn in on November 10 without a new government in place, after the October 27 vote cost Netanyahu his majority but left his rivals without a clear route to power. President Isaac Herzog has asked Eisenkot to form a government, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to assemble a government under his 28-day mandate, with the option of a 14-day extension. Should he fail, Netanyahu will get a chance to try, and if neither succeeds, Israel will go to another election next year, Reuters reported.
Netanyahu's Likud alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties secured 53 of the 120 Knesset seats, short of a majority of 61. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar and its potential partners, Lieberman's party among them, hold 48.
Arab parties, which have 19 seats and share Eisenkot's opposition to Netanyahu, could give his bloc a path to a majority.
Yashar and Israel Our Home won 21 and seven seats, respectively. The deal comes despite Lieberman's earlier objections to a government reliant on Arab party support or to joining a unity government with Netanyahu. Lieberman has repeatedly said his main goal is to remove Netanyahu from power.
Talks are also under way between Eisenkot, some members of the so-called change bloc and Likud on a possible unity government. Separately, the left-wing Democrats party, which holds eight seats, announced it was suspending negotiations with Eisenkot, citing his progress in talks with Likud and a stalemate in efforts to form a change government. Party leader Yair Golan has said he favours a government without Netanyahu that includes Arab parties.

title: Landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore as rent, filed ITR and slotted it as ‘Income from House Property’, but taxman reclassifies it as business income and raises taxable income to Rs 1.07 crore; why ITAT Surat gave relief
description: You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?
author: TOI Business Desk
content:
You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?
In one case, a landlord earned rent from and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) issued him a notice and classified the rental receipts as business income.
What the case is about
A landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head.
However, the AO reclassified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from the Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.
The sharp increase resulted from the change in the tax treatment of his rental earnings. Under the “Income from House Property” head, taxpayers can claim a flat standard deduction of 30% on the net annual value after deducting eligible municipal taxes paid.
When rental receipts are assessed as business income, however, taxpayers can claim eligible business expenses incurred to earn that income. This difference in the deductions available explains why the landlord’s taxable income rose from Rs 24.07 lakh to Rs 1.07 crore.
The landlord calculated that if his rental earnings of around Rs 2.7 crore were assessed as income from house property, he would be entitled to claim Rs 81.52 lakh as a standard deduction under Section 24, along with Rs 1.63 lakh for municipal taxes he had paid, according to an ET report on the judgement.
By treating the rent as business income, the AO denied the landlord the benefit of the deductions available under the house-property head. The CIT (Appeals) subsequently upheld the AO’s decision.
The landlord then challenged the order before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Surat. On November 4, 2026, he won on the key question of how his rental income should be classified for tax purposes.
Why did ITAT Surat give relief to landlord?
The landlord’s business involves dealing in land and constructing buildings. He earned rent from industrial buildings that formed part of his stock-in-trade, or business assets. The Assessing Officer relied on this aspect while assessing the rental receipts under the head “Income from Business or Profession”.
The landlord, however, maintained that his business was the “business of dealing in lands and construction of buildings”, and not the “business of letting out buildings”.
ITAT Surat held that the fact that he dealt in land, constructed buildings and rented out properties held as stock-in-trade for sale did not, by itself, settle the question of how the rental receipts should be classified. The determining factor was the nature of the activity from which the income arose.
The tribunal referred to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Chennai Properties and Investments Ltd. (supra), in which rental income was treated as business income because letting out properties was itself the assessee’s business.
However, ITAT Surat distinguished that ruling, along with the other judgments relied upon by the CIT (Appeals), on the ground that those cases involved taxpayers whose business was letting out properties.
The tribunal also noted that the Gujarat High Court’s ruling in Commissioner of Income-tax v. New India Industries Ltd. (1993) 201 ITR 208 (Guj) supported the landlord’s contention that his rental earnings were taxable under the head “Income from House Property”.
The tribunal further observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that the landlord was engaged in the business of letting out properties. It also noted that no material had been placed before it to establish that he was carrying on such a business.
Chartered Accountant Chintan Ghelani told ET that the landlord’s case succeeded because ITAT Surat distinguished between conducting a real-estate business and carrying on a business of letting out properties.
Ghelani explained that rent earned from industrial buildings cannot automatically be classified as business income merely because those properties are held as stock-in-trade, or business assets.
Under income tax law, rental earnings from letting out properties, including buildings, are ordinarily taxable as house-property income under Section 22. However, such receipts may be assessed as business income if the facts establish that letting out properties is itself the taxpayer’s business.
In this case, ITAT Surat observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that he was engaged in the business of letting out properties. Nor had any material been brought before the tribunal to establish that this was the nature of his business.
Ghelani also pointed out that Section 23(5) expressly recognises that a property forming part of stock-in-trade can still come within the scope of the house-property provisions. Therefore, while the classification of a property as stock-in-trade is relevant, it does not, by itself, determine the tax head under which its rental income must be assessed.
In its order, ITAT Surat ruled in favour of the landlord on the classification of his rental income, holding that the Rs 2.73 crore received from industrial buildings held as stock-in-trade was taxable under the head “Income from House Property” and not “Income from Business or Profession”.
The tribunal directed the Assessing Officer to recompute his income under the house-property head, allow deductions admissible under the Income Tax Act and grant consequential relief in accordance with the law.
It also directed the AO to ensure that expenses were not deducted twice under different heads of income.

title: ‘I don't know what you're talking about’: US attorney general dodges questions on Jensen Huang, backs Nvidia CEO as ‘good corporate citizen’
description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has described Nvidia as a \"good corporate citizen\" while declining to clarify whether the artificial intelligence
author: Ayush Pandey
content:
US Attorney General Todd Blanche has described Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while declining to clarify whether the artificial intelligence chipmaker or its newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang is facing a federal investigation.
Blanche also said he had no information about Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers seek answers over President Donald Trump's involvement in the CEO's return to the company and potential national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business dealings with China.
Asked repeatedly on Tuesday whether the Justice Department or the FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche said: "I don't know what you're talking about."
Huang is scheduled to appear before Congress next week, where lawmakers are expected to question him about national security concerns linked to his relationship with a Chinese woman suspected of having intelligence connections. The woman reportedly headed Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.
The US Commerce Department has also announced plans to blacklist Megaspeed over suspicions that the company helped divert advanced semiconductor chips to China.
In a joint statement last week, the Commerce and Justice departments said they had launched an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
However, Blanche said the Justice Department was handling a large number of export-related investigations at any given time.
"So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.
Asked whether Nvidia had cooperated with efforts to establish whether the company or Huang knew about the alleged diversion of chips to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.
"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.
"It shouldn't be what my message would be either."
Nvidia shares retreat after sharp rally
Meanwhile, Nvidia shares fell nearly 6% on Tuesday, reversing some of the gains recorded after Huang's reinstatement as CEO. Despite the decline, the stock remained above its closing level from the previous week.
The company's shares had surged more than 31% on Monday following the announcement that its board had reinstated Huang in a surprise reversal.
Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said the decision was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".
The board also said it had received input from senior US government officials and was confident that Huang's return would not pose a national security risk.
Trump had earlier claimed that he spoke to Nvidia's directors and persuaded them to bring Huang back. The president subsequently said he was open to pardoning Huang if necessary, describing it as "always an option", although he added that he did not expect it to be required.
Bipartisan criticism over Trump's role
Huang's reinstatement has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, with lawmakers questioning Trump's intervention and the potential national security implications.
Republican Congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".
Republican Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".
On the Democratic side, Congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" in Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".
Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego also called for congressional scrutiny, saying lawmakers needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

title: Selector must have stature, not just a seat at the table: Dilip Vengsarkar
description: At a time when India’s team selection has come under scrutiny following the controversial calls involving Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja in
author: Nitin Naik
content:
At a time when India’s team selection has come under scrutiny following the controversial calls involving 
Mohammed Siraj
 and 
Ravindra Jadeja
 in Wellington, former India captain and chief selector 
Dilip Vengsarkar
 believes the solution lies not merely in having a selector travel with the team, but in ensuring that the men doing the job have the stature to challenge the captain and coach.
Vengsarkar, widely regarded as one of India’s finest chairmen of selectors, feels the travelling selector cannot simply be an observer. He should be part of the process of choosing the playing XI and, crucially, be strong enough to intervene when he believes the team management is getting a major call wrong.
“When I was chairman of the selection committee, if any member of the five-man committee went on a tour, he would chair the selection meeting along with the captain and vice-captain. The meeting would be convened by the manager,” Vengsarkar told TOI.
“So, automatically, the selector chairing the meeting had a say in the playing XI. The meeting should involve the selector, coach, captain and vice-captain and be convened by the manager,” he stated.
With Shubman Gill still inexperienced in his job as Test captain, should the selection committee then carry greater responsibility over what XI plays?
Vengsarkar believes the captain’s age or experience is not necessarily the issue here.
“It depends on the stature of the person who is the selector there on tour. If a person without stature accompanies the team, he can be influenced or dominated,” he said.
During Vengsarkar’s stint as chief selector, his panel included Venkatapathy Raju, Ranjib Biswal, Bhupinder Singh Sr and Sanjay Jagdale. Vengsarkar says he and Jagdale chaired selection meetings when they travelled with the team.
He recalled an episode from a tour which, without naming the captain or coach involved, illustrated why a strong selector could become an important balancing presence.
“The coach told me to sort things out because he felt slighted as the captain was not consulting him at all while picking the XI. I sat beside the captain and told him, ‘I will chair the meeting, along with you and the vice-captain, and let the manager convene it.’ The captain immediately agreed and said, ‘If you are chairing the meeting, I have no issues.’”
For Vengsarkar, the danger in leaving the playing XI entirely to the captain and coach is that the two are always closely aligned. That can leave little room for a dissenting view. “If you give the power to pick the XI only to the coach and captain, they generally are always on the same page. That gives them room to bring in their personal likes and dislikes. Let the selector on tour be the neutral voice. If it is a 50-50 call, the selector should always go with the captain. But if you spot something blatantly wrong, he must put his foot down.”
Vengsarkar insists this is not an issue restricted to the present set-up. Previous captain-coach combinations, he says, have also enjoyed unhinged power.
Without identifying players, he recalled how a cricketer who had scored heavily in an important tournament was relegated to 12th-man duties in the next series because he was viewed as competition for the captain. He cited another instance of a Test cricketer who stood in as captain, won an important Test and soon found himself on the bench. “I would not have allowed it,” he says.
As India captain, Vengsarkar did not have the luxury of touring selectors, not least because the BCCI did not have its present financial muscle. “Especially when a series was happening in the West Indies, selectors would not travel. I would ask my vice-captain and another senior player to sit in the meeting along with the manager,” he recalled.
His tenure as chief selector also showed that a robust selection structure need not mean confrontation between selector and captain. “There were a lot of questions around Virender Sehwag’s selection for the 2007-08 Australia tour. He had not been part of the England tour earlier that year. But Anil Kumble and I were on the same page and we picked him as the 17th member, despite another opener having scored more runs than him in domestic cricket,” Vengsarkar said.
Ultimately, Vengsarkar believes the quality and independence of the individual matter more than merely putting a selector on the plane. “It has become such a lucrative job that sometimes many prefer to stay quiet, take their package and avoid rocking the boat with the coach, captain or board when it comes to selecting or dropping players.”

title: Trump set to hit India, China, 14 others with new tariffs after probe
description: NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union,
author: TNN
content:
NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union, the US Trade Representative is all set to unveil its findings in the case and propose tariffs.
The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week, with Bloomberg reporting that it may come in as early as Tuesday. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe, which is likely to be followed by a set of hearings, before final tariffs are announced, in around 45 days.
After the setback in the US Supreme Court over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump administration had launched two probes under Section 301.
Section 301 probe: Govt doesn’t expect any negative impact
While additional tariffs of 10-12.5 per cent were imposed on imports from over 50 countries, including India, for their alleged failure to prohibit the import of goods with forced labour, which harmed American exports, the outcome of the second investigation is awaited.
Going by the mood here, the government does not expect any negative impact, although it maintains that there is no structural excess capacity in India and the surplus is in anticipation of higher demand in the world’s fastest-growing major economy. 
In fact, during deliberations with the US government too, officials have made it clear that the government has not provided subsidy or other support to create capacity, while underlining that any country which has surplus domestic production is engaged in exports.
The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. In the first probe, India had managed to get concessions with the final levy of 10 per cent imposed, against 12.5 per cent, proposed initially. The outcome of the investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework, although the final levy will be known in around 45 days. Based on the final tariff, governments will engage in negotiations for “trade deals”. India is confident of negotiating a deal where its exports enjoy “comparative advantage” over rivals from the region.
While the first set of tariffs related to forced labour have been challenged in US courts, even the second one is expected to face litigation, especially because USTR findings are similar for almost all countries. In the case of structural excess capacity, among the top 20 trading partners for the US, all except Canada, the UK, Brazil and Australia are facing action, with the large European countries being part of the EU. The list also includes Norway, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, which are not among the top 20 partners for goods and services trade.

title: Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained
description: FSSAI moves to prosecute Bisleri after unsafe bromate and PAH findings prompt tougher rules for India’s packaged drinking water.
author: Kartikey  Singh
content:
The story so far: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the country’s apex food-safety regulator, sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. after a sample of its water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards, with the regulator declaring it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The public-health stakes are significant. In 2023, bottled water was the principal source of drinking water for 15% of urban and 6% of rural households, as per Data For India. For consumers buying it at railway stations, airports, highway eateries and neighbourhood shops, a sealed bottle is often taken as an assurance of safety. Yet, the data submitted in Parliament in February 2025 revealed that 333 of 1,300 enforcement samples of packaged drinking water tested in 2023-24 failed to meet prescribed standards. Similarly, in 2022-23, 650 of 1,776 samples had been found non-compliant.
According to the FSSAI, a sample of packaged drinking water (other than mineral water) collected from Bisleri’s premises was found to be non-compliant with the prescribed limits for “bromate” and was declared unsafe under the 2006 Act. Following an appeal by the food business operator (FBO), the sample was referred to a Referral Food Laboratory for further examination, which also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of “polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons” (PAHs).
In its response, Bisleri has maintained that its water is safe for consumption, saying the matter concerned a batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025, one of 143 manufacturing plants in its network. In a statement issued on November 23, the company said the FSSAI had collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. While five samples met the prescribed standards, the sixth recorded a “bromate” level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Further, Bisleri said it appealed on November 22, 2025, following which the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting. The laboratory, as claimed, found the bromate level within the prescribed limit but separately detected PAHs. Citing the divergent test findings, the company reportedly arranged an independent examination of the same sample at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which, according to Bisleri, also found the bromate level within limits. The company said it submitted these results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office on February 2, 2026, but received no further communication and understood that the matter had been closed.
Water is essential for digestion, blood circulation, temperature regulation and kidney function, but its safety cannot be judged by its appearance, taste, odour or sealed packaging alone. Contamination may be microbiological, causing illnesses such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid, or chemical, with some substances posing risks through prolonged exposure. In India, packaged water broadly falls into two categories: (1) “packaged drinking water”, which may be sourced from surface water, groundwater or seawater and treated through processes such as filtration, decantation, reverse osmosis (RO) and disinfection; and (2) “natural mineral water”, drawn from protected underground sources and characterised by a relatively stable mineral composition. Both must meet prescribed chemical and microbiological safety standards.

title: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s manufacturing licences again over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious
description: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s licences again for nine unauthorised, spurious drugs, with ₹1.72 crore stock seized and possible Prosecution.
author: Yohaan Varghese
content:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.
The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested.
The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders.
The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs.
Earlier violations
The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content.
Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4.
Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products.
Risk to patients
A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23.
The licensing authority rejected the firm’s contention that no patient complaints had been received, observing that the risk of treatment failure arising from spurious and substandard drugs existed even in the absence of complaints.
“Ensuring that citizens have access to safe, quality and efficacious drugs is the foremost responsibility of the Food and Drug Administration. Stringent regulatory and legal action will be taken against any manufacturer who plays with the health of the general public by manufacturing drugs without product permission,” FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said.

title: Behind Ramdev-Dhirendra Shastri exchange, a jockeying for relevance in poll-bound U.P.
description: Two BJP-linked religious figures, Dhirendra Shastri and Baba Ramdev, clash over Ram-Krishna comparisons amid UP poll maneuvering.
author: Ishita Mishra
content:
Two ‘babas’, both perceived as close to the BJP, are facing off as religious and political activities gain pace in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. Even before the political backlash over his comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna could die down, Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri faced thinly veiled criticism from yoga guru Baba Ramdev, who on Monday (November 23, 2026) called those who draw such analogies “hypocrites”.
Mr. Shastri shied away from escalating the exchange, but the spat has drawn attention as the political plot thickens in India’s most populous State. Political observers see the exchange against the backdrop of caste equations in Uttar Pradesh and Mr. Ramdev’s bid to remain in relevance as a 30-year-old gains increasing traction with his religious discourses in the Hindi heartland.
Mr. Shastri, no stranger to controversy, waded into the latest one with comments made during a religious gathering in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri on October 29 where he contrasted a “crooked” Lord Krishna with Lord Ram, who “stands absolutely straight, looks straight and walks straight”. The comments riled Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, both of whom lean heavily on the Yadavs, who trace their lineage to Yaduvanshis and Lord Krishna. The SP chief even demanded a board prohibiting the entry of such people into Uttar Pradesh be put up at the Madhya Pradesh border.
Although Mr. Shastri subsequently apologised for hurting devotees’ sentiments, the controversy got second wind on Monday when Mr. Ramdev offered his take during a religious event in Jamshedpur. “Those who made comparisons between gods and goddesses – ‘Ram is great, Krishna is crooked’ – and later apologised are hypocrites... Nobody in society has the right to say such petty things. There is decorum, discipline and protocol for everything,” he said without naming anyone.
Mr. Shastri chose to pipe down in response, describing Mr. Ramdev as his “senior and guardian”. On cue, the yoga guru, in Haridwar on Tuesday, softened his position, calling Mr. Shastri his “younger brother” and saying his criticism “came out of affection”.
The two have shared platforms in the past, including at BJP national media in-charge Anil Baluni’s Deepavali-linked celebration in Delhi on November 20. Days earlier, Mr. Ramdev also attended a Ram Katha (discourse) in Kunda, U.P., headlined by Mr. Shastri that was organised by Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, a seven-term MLA and founder of the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik). It was attended by several prominent political figures, including Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, Minister Suresh Khanna, former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, former Union Minister Sanjeev Balyan and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey.
While Mr. Shastri emerges as a prominent face of a younger generation of Hindu preachers, attracting large crowds to his religious congregations and building a substantial social media following, Mr. Ramdev has seen his once prominent public profile face challenges. One of the key supporters during the BJP’s rise to power in 2014, he built a national identity around yoga, nationalism and Patanjali Ayurved. In recent years, however, he has faced backlash over Supreme Court proceedings pertaining to his company’s misleading advertisements.
As a preacher-on-the-rise and a veteran yoga guru jostle for influence, the BJP’s efforts to marshal a spectrum of castes and communities to prevail in a high-voltage election means cultivating both – the first a Brahmin and other a Yadav.
“Many of those who have made such statements in the past have faced legal action and even arrests. As nothing of this sort has happened here, it shows that the Baba (Mr. Shastri) may have ruling party’s support. But how the BJP is going to handle this matter where two of its own poster boys are fighting will be interesting to watch,” said Shashi Kant Pandey, who teaches political science at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Central University in Lucknow.

title: Woman gang-raped by colleagues at east Delhi cafe; three arrested
description: Delhi cafe gang-rape: police arrest three, two women among suspects; victims and perpetrators linked to late-night party at multiple locations.
author: Lavpreet Kaur
content:
A 22-year-old woman was allegedly gang-raped by two male colleagues during a late-night gathering at a cafe in east Delhi’s Preet Vihar in the early hours of Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
The police arrested three people, including two women, in connection with the case. Three other accused are on the run and efforts are under way to trace them, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East) Rajeev Kumar said.
According to the officer, the woman and the six accused worked at another cafe in a mall near Karkardooma Court. All six persons are Delhi residents who worked as attendants and waiters at the cafe.
After their workplace shut on Monday night (November 23, 2026), the group decided to party and first consumed alcohol before heading to the residence of one of the colleagues in Mandawali, where they allegedly consumed more alcohol.
The "party” continued into the early hours of Tuesday (November 24, 2026). At around 2.30 a.m., they returned to Preet Vihar and went to Saltanate Cafe, which had shut for the night at around 11.30 p.m.
“One of the men had previously worked at the establishment and was aware about where the keys were kept. He contacted its caretaker to confirm the location of the keys. The group then gained access to the cafe and continued drinking,” Mr. Kumar added.
Around 3.30 a.m., the three women left with a male friend of the victim, who had arrived to pick her up. The men left for their respective homes, as per the CCTV footage checked by the police.
At around 6 a.m., the victim, accompanied by her male friend, approached the police and alleged that two of her male colleagues had sexually assaulted her during the gathering and that the group had assisted them in the crime.
A case was then registered under the relevant provisions relating to gang rape.

title: Arrangements in place for Mission Chakkakompan; Kerala Forest dept to tranquilize wild tusker
description: Forest department plans to dart and collar Chakkakompan, aims to collar Murivali, with security measures and drill for Mission Chakkakompan in Chinnakkanal.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
As the Forest Department and district administration completed arrangements on Tuesday to tranquilize and fit a radio collar to Chakkakompan at Chinnakkanal in the Devikulam forest range on Wednesday, officials said they are also planning to fit a radio collar to Murivali, another “problematic” wild elephant in the area.
District Collector has issued prohibitory orders in several wards of the Chinnakkanal panchayat ahead of the operation, officials said.
According to Chief Conservator of Forests D.K. Vinod Kumar, the mission is expected to take place on Wednesday once the elephant approaches Vilakku in Chinnakkanal.
“Officials have been directed to identify additional spots in the area to conduct the operation,” Mr. Kumar said. “After the mission, the team will remain in Chinnakkanal for two more days as it plans to attach a radio collar to Murivali, another problematic female elephant. A proposal to dart Murivali will be submitted to the Chief Wildlife Warden. The animal is currently in Mathikettan Shola and needs to move toward Chinnakkanal before we can conduct the operation.”
Two high-quality radio collars were sourced from abroad, he said.
Mr. Kumar noted that a study by a Professor at the Wildlife Institute of India found that wild elephants’ aggressive behaviour decreases after they are fitted with radio collars.
Elephants are now getting aggressive, increasing human–elephant conflicts. Wild elephants in Chinnakkanal have reached an aggressive level, said Mr. Kumar.
Threat assessment
He added that installing the radio collar is the first step, and if the animal continues to pose a threat, the Forest department will take further action to translocate it from the Chinnakkanal region.
Two kumkis (trained elephants) named Vikram and Bharat have arrived in Chinnakkanal to assist with the operation, officials said. On Tuesday, the Forest department conducted a mock drill at Cement Palam, near Chinnakkanal, ahead of Mission Chakkakompan. Munnar Divisional Forest Officer Saju Varghese led the drill, which included an expert team, veterinary doctors and Rapid Response Team members.
As part of Mission Chakkakompan, the District Collector declared a holiday on Wednesday for schools, tuition centers and anganwadis in wards 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 and 12 of the Chinnakkanal panchayat. The Collector also banned night camps and campfires in those wards on Wednesday.
According to officials, the mission is expected to begin from 6 a.m. onwards. Two Kumki elephants, along with a 100-member team, will lead the operation. Five veterinary doctors and a 15-member tracking team are also part of the group. The tusker was camped in the 80-acre area until Tuesday evening, when it started moving toward the 301 Colony area. Officials expect to bring the animal to an open space near Cement Palam.
An official said that mission-related equipment has been stored at Chinnakkanal Fathima Matha School, with two sets of each piece of equipment kept as a backup for the mission..

title: Kerala HC declines to interfere with State govt’s reconstitution of Waqf Board
description: Kerala HC won't halt the state’s reconstitution of the Waqf Board, noting the board was already functional.
author: PTI
content:
The Kerala High Court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) declined to interfere with the Keralam government’s decision to reconstitute the State Waqf Board, saying that it was already functional.
A Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing appeals by K S Hamza and C K Usman Haji, the former chairperson and member of the earlier board that was disbanded barely eight months into its five-year term, against a single judge order declining to stay the reconstitution of the board.
The single judge, on October 17, had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board but said that it would be subject to the outcome of the petitions challenging the same.
The judge had also tagged the petitions by Hamza and Haji with the earlier PILs – challenging the validity of the previous and now disbanded board – which were pending before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Soumen Sen.
However, the Bench headed by the Chief Justice on October 19 dismissed the PILs as the board had been reconstituted.
On Tuesday, the Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji directed the Registry that the earlier petitions of Hamza and Haji be listed before the appropriate Bench.

title: No power can harm India as long as it reveres Sikh Gurus, says U.P. CM Adityanath
description: Yogi Adityanath emphasizes reverence for Sikh Gurus as India's shield, highlighting Guru Nanak's teachings for unity, equality, and national harmony.
author: Mayank Kumar
content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said that no power in the world will be able to harm India as long as it continues to hold Sikh Gurus in reverence and respect.
“The sacrifice, penance, martyrdom, and spiritual consciousness of the Sikh Gurus are invaluable treasures of India’s national unity, social harmony, and cultural pride,” Mr. Adityanath said, addressing a program organised on the occasion of the 557th Prakash Parv of Sahib Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Lucknow .
“Through ‘Ek Onkar’, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj gave the message of uniting all humanity. His teachings remain as relevant today as they were then. We must not confine these teachings to events and celebrations alone, but imbibe them in our lives and continuously familiarize the younger generation with them as well,” he added.
Referring to the spiritual and religious significance of Kartik Purnima, the U.P. Chief Minister said, “Today is an extremely sacred day for entire state. Since 4 am, I have been receiving updates on the number of devotees and arrangements at various religious sites across the state. At Shukratal in Muzaffarnagar, lakhs of devotees are taking a holy dip in the Ganga.
At Garhmukteshwar in Hapur, approximately 15 lakh devotees took a holy dip on Tuesday. Meanhwhile, more than 15 lakh devotees took a dip of faith in the Ganga at Tigri in Amroha. A large number of devotees also arrived in Prayagraj and Farrukhabad, while lakhs of them visited the Ganga in Ayodhya and Kashi,”.
Referring to the journeys undertaken by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and social conditions prevailing during his time, Mr. Adityanath said, “When he conveyed the message of unity to humanity, society was grappling with numerous social evils and divisions. Society was fragmented in the name of caste, untouchability and discrimination.
At the same time, he said foreign invasions and external attacks posed challenges. During such difficult times, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj united all humanity through the mantra of ‘Ek Onkar’. His clear message was that God is one and we are all His children. Therefore, every human being deserves equal respect. This mantra, given by him, became a great force for uniting society at that time, and it remains relevant even today. Despite limited means and resources, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj traveled to various places and spread the message of humanity, equality and spiritual consciousness among the masses,”.
Explaining the three principal teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj, ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako’, the U.P. CM added, “Remembering God, performing kirtan and embracing the spirit of togetherness generate positive feelings within human beings. This dispels ignorance and awakens the strength of unity in society,”..

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will open ‘Vision Koyilandy Conclave 2026’, an event to chalk out future development plans for the Koyilandy Assembly constituency in Kozhikode district, on November 27.
Koyilandy MLA and Kozhikode District Congress Committee president K. Praveenkumar told the media on Tuesday (November 24) that the event would be held at the Koyilandy stadium. He said that the aim was to conceive projects in sectors such as education, health, transport, agriculture, industry, tourism, and infrastructure development. Experts in various fields would discuss their ideas at the conclave. “We want to prepare a development plan for the constituency for 2040. A development blueprint will be prepared based on the suggestions raised at the conclave within a month after the event,” Mr. Praveenkumar said.
A two-day exhibition showcasing the various development projects being taken up in the constituency would begin on Wednesday (November 25). Kerala Sahitya Akademi chairperson Kalpetta Narayanan would open the exhibition. Apart from the Chief Minister, Ministers such as N. Samsudheen, A.P. Anil Kumar, V.E. Abdul Gafoor, and T. Siddique, and Shafi Parambil and P.T. Usha, MPs, would attend the conclave along with elected representatives from municipalities, grama panchayats, district panchayats, and block panchayats, Mr. Praveenkumar said. Chairpersons of Payyoli and Koyilandy municipalities and grama panchayat presidents in the constituency were present at the press meet.
Meanwhile, the Koyilandy MLA claimed that the United Democratic Front-led government had sanctioned at least 16 projects for the constituency in the past six months. Preliminary works have already begun. Apart from them, a proposal had been given to develop a mini cruise terminal at Kolavipalam. Asked about the poor condition of roads leading to Kappad, a historically important place in the constituency, Mr. Praveenkumar said that a project had been prepared to construct a breakwater between Kannankadavu and Kolavipalam. It would address the issue of roads getting damaged in the monsoon season, he added.

title: ‘Will take Bangladesh by Dec 16’: Bengal minister’s controversial remark amid tensions over alleged Hindu killings | India News
description: Sheikh Hasina's spokesperson said that the former PM intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier. | India News
author: ANI
content:
‘Will take Bangladesh by Dec 16’: Bengal minister’s controversial remark amid tensions over alleged Hindu killings
Sheikh Hasina's spokesperson said that the former PM intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier.
West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that the country would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country would be "avenged".
Speaking to reporters in Bhatpara, he made a controversial remark about Bangladesh on Tuesday, saying, "We will take Bangladesh by December 16th. Enough is enough; there are no more excuses regarding Bangladesh. We will certainly take revenge for the way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh; there is no doubt about that."
His remarks came amid tensions in Bangladesh, where the country's State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kobir, earlier said that former Prime Minister and Awami League chief Sheikh Hasina would only be allowed to return to the country as a prisoner, in handcuffs and under strict surveillance.
Deep Dive
Kobir reportedly made the remarks while addressing journalists after briefing foreign diplomats at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka. Dismissing Hasina's reported plan to return to Bangladesh from India on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations, he said, "Desire and reality are two different things."
"The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition... She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," The Business Standard quoted Kobir as saying.
Earlier, Hasina's spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, had informed Reuters that the former Prime Minister intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
In an official communication, Ali said that Hasina had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration for her return journey. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters.
Separately, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam reportedly described Hasina's demand for a state aircraft to facilitate her return as "nothing but madness".
Meanwhile, A Bangladeshi minister had informed Reuters on Sunday that Hasina faced immediate arrest and imprisonment if she returned, noting that no formal talks had taken place with India regarding the dispatch of a plane for her travel.
Hasina, who led Bangladesh as prime minister from 2009 until 2024, arrived in India on August 5, 2024, in the wake of a student-led agitation over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her Awami League administration.
She was later handed a death sentence in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal over charges of crimes against humanity linked to the suppression of protesters, allegations that Hasina has denied.
Hasina initially declared her wish to return to Bangladesh at a virtual media briefing in August this year and has repeated those plans during several subsequent interviews. Earlier this month, she also applied for a new passport and national identity card through legal representatives in the United Kingdom.
Dhaka has made repeated requests to India for her extradition, while New Delhi has maintained that the matter is under examination.

title: 6-year-old boy dies after falling from 11th floor of Maharashtra building: Police | India News
description: The incident took place at Navkar Tower Society in Naigaon East when the boy was playing with a girl in the corridor outside his flat. | India News
author: Megha Sood
content:
6-year-old boy dies after falling from 11th floor of Maharashtra building: Police
The incident took place at Navkar Tower Society in Naigaon East when the boy was playing with a girl in the corridor outside his flat.
Updated on: Nov 25, 2026, 09:30:19 IST
By
Megha Sood
Share via
Copy link
A six-year-old boy died after falling from the 11th floor of a residential building in Maharashtra’s Palghar district on Tuesday, police said.
The incident took place at Navkar Tower Society in Naigaon East when the boy was playing with a girl in the corridor outside his flat. A preliminary probe suggested the boy lost his balance near a window and fell. He first hit a fire-safety pipe, before hitting the ground, the police said.
He was rushed to Cardinal Gracias Hospital in Vasai but succumbed to injuries during treatment.
The police have registered an accidental death report.
Local residents alleged lack of safety grills in the windows along the corridors.
“We have repeatedly requested the installation of the safety grills but the builder has ignored these demands. We have also raised concerns about the poor condition of the society’s lifts. One wing’s lift is currently out of service,” a resident said, seeking anonymity.
There was no immediate comment from the society authorities at the time of filing this report.
Local residents said the boy lost his mother 15 days ago. His father reportedly planned to send him to a hostel in Mahabaleshwar.
The police said they are yet to record the father’s statement in the case.

title: Keralam to increase women's representation in police force to 30 per cent: Minister Chennithala | India News
description: Keralam to increase women's representation in police force to 30 per cent: Minister Chennithala | India News
author: PTI
content:
Keralam to increase women's representation in police force to 30 per cent: Minister Chennithala
Malappuram , Keralam will increase women's representation in the police force to 30 per cent through phased recruitment, while introducing reforms to improve the efficiency of the Crime Branch and Vigilance wings, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said.
In future recruitments, women will be inducted in a 7:3 ratio, following a Cabinet decision to enhance their representation in the force, he said.
Women officers were performing well in crime detection and anti-drug operations, Chennithala said after inaugurating the newly constructed Malappuram Crime Branch unit office here on Tuesday.
At present, women officers serve as Station House Officers in 63 police stations across the state, he said.
The home minister said appointments to the Crime Branch and Vigilance wings are now being made purely on merit, with officers having an aptitude for investigation selected through a special examination.
The examination was devised in consultation with the Director General of Police and the Additional DGP , he said, adding that these specialised wings were not meant to accommodate officers who were sidelined due to workload in the regular police force.
The Crime Branch is currently handling 2,763 important cases, including 321 registered during 2026 alone. The department's priority was to complete investigations within a stipulated timeframe, he said.
Chennithala said 'Operation Toofan', launched to curb the spread of narcotic drugs in the state, has been a major success, with criminal cases witnessing a 35 per cent decline following its implementation.
As part of the drive, 17,351 cases had been registered and 16,593 people arrested so far, he said, particularly appreciating the Manjeri and Malappuram police teams for recently travelling to Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu and seizing 15 kg of MDMA.
Methylenedioxymethamphetamine , commonly known as ecstasy or molly, is a banned psychoactive substance.
He said the anti-drug operation had helped bring down criminal cases by 35 per cent in six months compared to the corresponding period of the previous year.
On addressing staff shortages and excessive workload at police stations, the minister said the government was considering deploying a fixed percentage of personnel from Armed Reserve camps and police battalions to police stations.
He also said steps were being taken to construct new buildings for police stations in Malappuram district that were functioning from rented premises, including those at Karipur, Edavanna, Edakkara, Pothukallu and Mankada.
Under the 'My Police Station' project, 90 per cent of police stations in the state had shifted to new buildings, which had been renovated with a uniform design and colour scheme, he said.
A dedicated software system had also been introduced to monitor, in real time, FIR registrations and serious crimes such as murder, robbery and missing-person cases, through a dashboard at the home minister's office.
The state had additionally secured ₹100 crore from the Centre for police modernisation, while 70 per cent of old vehicles piled up in front of police stations had already been removed, he said.
Announcing a further initiative, Chennithala said the old vehicles parked in front of the Malappuram police station would be cleared, and the space would be handed over to the municipality for beautification.
He said investigations into crimes, including murder cases, were progressing in a manner that would enable the police to identify offenders and bring them to justice, irrespective of how much time had elapsed since the offence.
The new Malappuram Crime Branch office building was constructed at ₹3.20 crore under the 2024-25 annual plan. Spread over 9,140 square feet, the two-storey facility has been built near the Malappuram police station to accommodate the unit, which was earlier functioning from two separate buildings.
The modern facility includes an investigation room, rooms for the Superintendent of Police and Deputy Superintendents of Police, a conference hall, Circle Inspector rooms, an administration office and other amenities, according to officials.
